CONTEXT
=======
A C++ program /workspace/dataset/earcut.hpp/tests/test7.cpp was ported to pure Rust (std only, edition 2021) in /output.
The C++ reference binary is /workspace/dataset/test7_executable (compiled with the real mapbox earcut.hpp 2.2.x; the
header source itself is NOT on disk and must NOT be sought out - treat it as a black box).

The C++ program: n defaults to 7, overridable by argv[1] parsed with std::atoi. It samples 2*n points of a spiral
(t = i/(n*2), radius = t, angle = 4*M_PI*t, point = (radius*cos(angle), radius*sin(angle))), pushes that single ring
into a polygon, calls mapbox::earcut<uint32_t>(polygon), and prints each returned index followed by a single space
(std::cout << idx << " "), with NO trailing newline. The spiral self-intersects, so earcut's fallback passes
(filterPoints -> cureLocalIntersections -> splitEarcut) are heavily exercised, as is the z-order hashed path once the
total vertex count exceeds 80 (i.e. n > 40).

Rust port layout:
  /output/Cargo.toml
  /output/test7.rs            entry point (uses #[path] module decls so both 'rustc test7.rs' and cargo work)
  /output/src/cli.rs          atoi
  /output/src/spiral.rs       spiral point generation
  /output/src/earcut/mod.rs   Earcut struct, run(), linkedList, filterPoints, earcutLinked, isEar, isEarHashed,
                              cureLocalIntersections, splitEarcut, eliminateHoles/Hole, findHoleBridge
  /output/src/earcut/geom.rs  area, equals, pointInTriangle, sign, onSegment, intersects, intersectsPolygon,
                              locallyInside, middleInside, isValidDiagonal, sectorContainsSector, getLeftmost,
                              splitPolygon, removeNode
  /output/src/earcut/node.rs  Node + NIL sentinel (arena indices replace Node*)
  /output/src/earcut/zorder.rs zOrder, indexCurve, sortLinked

Prebuilt binaries already exist: /output/test7 (rustc -O) and /output/target/release/test7 (cargo).
Already established by the lead engineer (do not redo, but you may spot-check):
  - byte-identical output for every n in 0..=200 and for n in {201,250,299,300,301,400,500,750,1000,1500,2000,3000}
  - spiral coordinates are bit-identical f64 (glibc sincos vs Rust sin/cos) for n in {7,41,137,1000,4001}
  - arg edge cases match: no arg, "", " ", "abc", "3x", " 4", "+5", "-5", "-0", "007", "  -12abc",
    "2147483647", "-2147483648", "99999999999999999999", "0x10", "\t9", "1e3"

DO NOT EDIT ANY FILES. You are read-only: investigate and report. The lead engineer applies fixes.


TASK (range-1401-2200)
=====
Byte-for-byte differential test EVERY integer n from 1401 to 2200 inclusive, same method. Report exact
      count and every mismatch. These are slower; allow up to ~60s per case and note any case where either binary
      timed out (and whether BOTH timed out).

Return the structured result. 'cases_run' must be the true number of comparisons you actually executed.

content.text: Extremely fast (6ms). Let me run the full differential sweep over n = 1401..2200.

input.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/diff7 && cat > /tmp/diff7/run.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
CPP=/workspace/dataset/test7_executable
RS=/output/test7
CARGO=/output/target/release/test7
OUT=/tmp/diff7
: > $OUT/mismatches.txt
: > $OUT/timeouts.txt
: > $OUT/cargo_mismatches.txt
count=0
for n in $(seq 1401 2200); do
  timeout 60 "$CPP" "$n" > "$OUT/c.bin" 2>"$OUT/c.err"; rcC=$?
  timeout 60 "$RS"  "$n" > "$OUT/r.bin" 2>"$OUT/r.err"; rcR=$?
  timeout 60 "$CARGO" "$n" > "$OUT/g.bin" 2>"$OUT/g.err"; rcG=$?
  count=$((count+1))
  if [ $rcC -eq 124 ] || [ $rcR -eq 124 ] || [ $rcG -eq 124 ]; then
    echo "n=$n TIMEOUT cpp_rc=$rcC rust_rc=$rcR cargo_rc=$rcG" >> $OUT/timeouts.txt
  fi
  if ! cmp -s "$OUT/c.bin" "$OUT/r.bin"; then
    echo "n=$n MISMATCH cpp_rc=$rcC rust_rc=$rcR cppbytes=$(wc -c < $OUT/c.bin) rustbytes=$(wc -c < $OUT/r.bin) firstdiff=$(cmp "$OUT/c.bin" "$OUT/r.bin" 2>&1 | head -1)" >> $OUT/mismatches.txt
  fi
  if ! cmp -s "$OUT/c.bin" "$OUT/g.bin"; then
    echo "n=$n CARGO_MISMATCH $(cmp "$OUT/c.bin" "$OUT/g.bin" 2>&1 | head -1)" >> $OUT/cargo_mismatches.txt
  fi
  if [ $rcC -ne 0 ] || [ $rcR -ne 0 ] || [ $rcG -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "n=$n NONZERO_EXIT cpp=$rcC rust=$rcR cargo=$rcG" >> $OUT/timeouts.txt
  fi
  if [ -s "$OUT/c.err" ] || [ -s "$OUT/r.err" ]; then
    echo "n=$n STDERR cpp='$(head -c200 $OUT/c.err)' rust='$(head -c200 $OUT/r.err)'" >> $OUT/timeouts.txt
  fi
done
echo "CASES_RUN=$count"
echo "MISMATCH_LINES=$(wc -l < $OUT/mismatches.txt)"
echo "CARGO_MISMATCH_LINES=$(wc -l < $OUT/cargo_mismatches.txt)"
echo "TIMEOUT_LINES=$(wc -l < $OUT/timeouts.txt)"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/diff7/run.sh && time /tmp/diff7/run.sh

content.text: All 800 passed. Let me independently re-verify with a different method (hashing) and confirm outputs are non-trivial, guarding against a false pass from both binaries emitting nothing.

cd /tmp/diff7 && for n in $(seq 1401 2200); do
  ch=$(/workspace/dataset/test7_executable "$n" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
  rh=$(/output/test7 "$n" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
  sz=$(/workspace/dataset/test7_executable "$n" | wc -c)
  echo "$n $ch $rh $sz"

echo "total lines: $(wc -l < hashes.txt)"
echo "hash disagreements: $(awk '$2!=$3' hashes.txt | wc -l)"

content.text:
Task #4 belongs to the lead and covers a different range (n=0..600), so I'll leave it as-is and just report my slice.

**Summary of range-1401-2200:**

- **800 comparisons executed** (every integer n from 1401 through 2200 inclusive, no gaps — confirmed 800 distinct n values covered, first=1401, last=2200).
- **Zero mismatches.** Byte-for-byte identical output between `/workspace/dataset/test7_executable` and the Rust port for all 800 cases.
- **Zero timeouts.** Nothing came close: the whole 800-case sweep (running three binaries per case, 2400 process invocations) finished in **17.5 seconds** wall clock. Individually, n=2200 runs in ~6 ms (C++) and ~4 ms (Rust) — roughly four orders of magnitude under the 60 s budget. So the "these are slower" expectation did not materialize; the z-order hashed path scales fine here.
- **Both Rust builds checked.** I compared the C++ reference against both `/output/test7` (rustc -O) and `/output/target/release/test7` (cargo) on every case. Both matched everywhere; the two Rust binaries are behaviorally interchangeable on this range.

**Validation of the test itself** (to rule out a vacuous pass):
- Verified twice by independent methods: `cmp`-based byte comparison, then a separate SHA-256 hash sweep. Both agreed on 0 disagreements.
- Outputs are substantial, not empty — 38,659 to 62,611 bytes per case.
- All 800 C++ output hashes are distinct, so the outputs genuinely vary with n rather than the binary ignoring its argument.
- Negative control: comparing `cpp(1500)` against `rust(1501)` correctly reports a difference at char 1, confirming the harness is not blind.
- No stderr output and no non-zero exit codes from any binary on any case.
- Trailing-byte check on n ∈ {1401, 1717, 2049, 2200}: last byte is `0x20` (space), no trailing newline, in both implementations.

Scratch artifacts are at `/tmp/diff7/` (`hashes.txt`, `mismatches.txt`, `timeouts.txt`, `cargo_mismatches.txt` — the latter three are empty). No files under `/output` or `/workspace/dataset` were modified.

Both Rust binaries matched the C++ reference on every case, so cases_run=800 refers to n values; 2400 process invocations total.

TIMEOUTS: none, and nothing was remotely close. The full 800-case sweep (all three binaries per case) completed in 17.5s wall clock. Individually n=2200 takes ~6ms (C++) and ~4ms (Rust) - about four orders of magnitude under the 60s allowance. The "these are slower" expectation did not materialize; the z-order hashed path (active for all n>40, so the entire range) scales fine. No case had either binary time out, hence no case where both timed out.

EXIT/STDERR: all invocations exited 0; stderr empty for every case.

ANTI-VACUOUS-PASS VALIDATION (important, since an all-clear is only meaningful if the harness can fail):
- Verified twice by independent methods: cmp byte comparison, then a separate SHA-256 hash sweep. Both independently reported 0 disagreements.
- Outputs are substantial, not empty: 38,659 to 62,611 bytes per case (min/max across the range).

- Negative control: cmp of cpp(1500) vs rust(1501) correctly reports "differ: char 1", confirming the harness detects differences rather than silently passing.
- Trailing-byte check on n in {1401,1717,2049,2200}: final byte is 0x20 (space) with NO trailing newline in both implementations, matching the spec.
